name: One incident, one case file
thesis: Every ERIS user, whatever their role, is really asking one question: 'what is happening with this incident and what do I do next?' Today the answer is scattered across five numbered objects (Incident #, Event Group #, Assessment #, Submission #, cross-section Project) on six read-only record pages plus a separate action inbox, so a newcomer has to learn the data model before they can do their job. This direction makes the Incident the only object a person navigates to. One role-aware case-file page per incident carries the field report, the Event Group context, the assessment routing (who has it, who is next), every technical form with its evidence, the site map/3D/cross sections, and a single timeline. Backend objects stay exactly as they are; they simply become tabs and cards inside the case file instead of destinations. Lists shrink to simple filterable card lists that open the case file, navigation collapses to Home / Incidents / Map (+ Admin), and every page states plainly where the incident is, who holds it, and what this user can do now. The result beats the measured baseline on every axis: content starts at ~100 px on phones instead of 700 px, no page except a map ever scrolls sideways, the 11-screen-tall 520 px form canvas becomes section pages under two screens each, and every control is 44 px on touch.

principles.name: One place per incident
principles.statement: Everything about an incident lives at /incidents/:id. Assessment, submissions, event-group context, evidence, terrain and history are tabs of that page, never separate destinations. Old URLs (/assessments/:id, /submissions/:id, /submissions/:id/photo-evidence, /mission-center/:gid/:iid) redirect into the right tab so deep links, emails and bookmarks keep working.

principles.name: Status, holder, next step, your move
principles.statement: Every case file, every list card and every Home item shows the same four facts in the same order: plain-language status, who holds it now (a named person where one exists), what happens next, and the one primary action available to the signed-in user. Raw codes (PENDING_OFFICE_DELEGATION, FIELD_WORKER, NORTH) never reach the screen.

principles.name: Place before numbers
principles.statement: An incident is identified first by its title and location line ('D7 · Los Angeles · Route 101 · PM 12.30'), then by its permanent key. Internal ids for assessments, submissions and users are demoted to muted text or hidden entirely; a chief chooses an engineer by where the site is, not by #12.

principles.name: Only what this page decides
principles.statement: Each tab and card shows the data needed for the decision made there and nothing else. Coordinates to six decimals, MIME types, SHA-256 fragments, event codes and duplicate counts move behind 'Details' disclosures or disappear. Lists carry at most five facts per card.

principles.name: Compose per breakpoint, never shrink
principles.statement: Four viewport size classes (compact <600, medium 600-839, expanded 840-1199, large >=1200) each get a designed composition: bottom bar / icon rail / sidebar; drill-in / two-pane; sheet / panel. Tables become card lists below 840; maps are one-per-screen and never trap page scroll on touch; 3D loads only on request.

principles.name: Consequence before commit, receipt after
principles.statement: Any action that changes ownership or is irreversible (accept, send to branch, assign, submit, approve, return, finalize, resolve, disable user, publish dataset) opens a small action sheet that names the target incident and person, states the consequence in one sentence, holds the note for that action, and after success leaves a receipt in the timeline and a notice on Home instead of silently removing the item.

navigation.model: Three destinations for everyone (Home, Incidents, Map) plus Admin for administrators, plus an always-visible avatar menu (name, humanized roles, Account & appearance, Help, Sign out). Maintenance reporters get Home and New report only (Map is server-restricted to operational roles). Assessments, Event Groups, Submissions, Mission Center, Terrain Cross Sections and Settings disappear as top-level items: assessments and submissions are tabs of the case file, Event Groups are a grouping/filter of the Incidents list and a light 'event page' reachable from any case file, terrain tools open from the case file's Site tab (or from the Map for ad-hoc use), Settings lives in the avatar menu. Nav badges: Home shows the count of items waiting on you; Incidents shows nothing (browse, not work).
navigation.desktop: Large (>=1200): persistent 240 px left sidebar with icon + label for Home / Incidents / Map / Admin, collapsible to a 64 px icon rail (state persisted in UiSettingsContext). Header is 56 px: ERIS mark (links to Home), page breadcrumb ('Incidents / Route 101 slide at PM 12.3'), global search (incident key, title, route/PM), Help button in a fixed slot (WCAG 3.2.6), avatar menu. No footer. Expanded (840-1199, e.g. iPad landscape, 13-inch split): 64 px icon rail by default with labels on hover/focus and an 'Expand' toggle; same header.
navigation.tablet: Medium (600-839, iPad portrait, half-width Split View): 64 px icon rail on the left (never a hamburger, never a stacked card), 56 px header with breadcrumb collapsed to the current page name, search behind an icon. Pages use drill-in (list replaces itself with detail) and the case file uses a horizontally scrollable tab strip. Map pages are full-height map with a bottom sheet list.
navigation.phone: Compact (<600): 56 px header (ERIS mark, page title, search icon, avatar) and a 56 px bottom tab bar with Home / Incidents / Map (/ Admin) — reporters see Home / New report. Content begins at 56 px (or 104 px under a sticky section heading) instead of today's 700 px. Detail pages replace the bottom bar with a sticky back header and a single sticky action bar at the bottom carrying the page's primary action. Filters, layer toggles and secondary actions open in bottom sheets.

navigation.rationale: The walkthroughs show newcomers cannot tell Mission Center, Event Groups, Incidents and Assessments apart because all four plausibly hold 'the status of an incident'. Collapsing to Home (what needs me), Incidents (look something up) and Map (where is it) matches the three questions people actually ask, stays under Apple's five-destination cap, and keeps the same three items on every device so the mental model does not change between an iPad in the field and a desk. Removing the hamburger and the stacked nav card recovers the first 700 px on phones and tablets (NN/g: hidden navigation is 20% less discoverable and 39% slower; the current stacked card is worse than either).

touchAndDensityRules: Every interactive element is at least 24x24 CSS px with 8 px spacing everywhere (WCAG 2.5.8) and at least 44x44 px under @media (pointer: coarse) — buttons, list rows, chips, radios/checkbox hit areas, map controls, thumbnails, tab items, sort headers.
Row density: 48 px on coarse pointers, 40 px default on fine pointers, 32 px compact only on fine pointers and only as a user choice persisted per user.

Minimum body text 14 px; captions 12 px minimum; no 9-11 px text anywhere (today's 23-74 tiny text nodes per page go to zero). Status badges: light background, dark text, 4.5:1 contrast, text + icon, never colour alone, never interactive.
Reflow: at 320 px width nothing outside a map or an explicitly horizontal table scrolls sideways; headers, filters, forms, dialogs and cards always reflow to one column.

Maps and 3D scenes never sit inside a scrolling container that also scrolls the page on touch: a map occupies its own region (full-height page or fixed-height block with page scroll controlled outside it); no nested scroll regions (no max-h + overflow-auto cards).

Hover is never the only affordance: links underlined, selected states use border + check glyph + aria-current/aria-pressed, tile actions are visible on hover:none devices, tooltips never carry required information.

Focus visible everywhere (2 px brand ring), skip-to-content link, live regions for notices (role=status) and errors (role=alert), dialogs with focus trap and restore (reuse ModalDialog), aria-current='step' on progress rails.

Layout breakpoints are viewport-based custom Tailwind v4 tokens (@theme --breakpoint-medium 600px, --breakpoint-expanded 840px, --breakpoint-large 1200px, --breakpoint-stack 480px); legacy sm/md/lg/xl remain for unmigrated pages and are removed page by page.

Pick 'J. Doe — North branch · 2 open · 14 mi' (2), optionally type a note to the engineer, press 'Assign J. Doe' (3).
Receipt toast 'Assigned to J. Doe — they are notified; next they complete the technical form'; the card moves to 'My branch in progress' and the case-file banner reads 'Engineer J. Doe working'.

referenceJourneys.task: Add a reviewer to an assessment
steps: On Home, 'Reviewer needed (1)' lists the same assessment (now a draft) with 'No reviewer assigned — review will be blocked'; tap 'Add reviewer' (1).

referenceJourneys.task: Check the status of an incident a district called me about
steps: Type 'I-80 PM 45' (or the incident key) into the header search (1); results show the card with status 'Under review — reviewer A. Patel · in this step 3 days'.
Open the case file (2): banner 'Under review — A. Patel has it. Next: they approve or return it.' and the progress rail with dates; nothing else needed.

referenceJourneys.task: Find the new field reports waiting for me today and accept one with the right Event Group and disposition
steps: Sign in → Home 'Needs my decision (3)' shows District 7 reports oldest first with photo thumbnail, reporter and 'Reported 2 h ago'.
Tap 'Review and decide' on a card (1) → case file Report tab opens with the intake sheet: step 1 lists nearby Event Groups by distance ('Suggested · 1.5 mi away', not preselected) beside the map.
Choose the suggested Event Group or 'Starts its own event' (2), press Continue (3).
Step 2: choose 'Accept for assessment' (4) — consequence line 'Routes to North GeoTech Office (District 7 → North)'; add a note; press 'Accept and send to North GeoTech Office' (5).
Receipt in the sheet, then the case file banner reads 'Accepted — with North GeoTech Office; office chief M. Ortiz is next'. Home now shows it under 'Recently accepted'.

referenceJourneys.task: Check what happened to a report I triaged last week
steps: On Home, expand 'Recently accepted (7 days)' (1): each row shows the decision I made and where it is now ('Accepted Sep 1 → Engineer J. Doe working'); 'Waiting on reporter' lists returned reports separately.
If older than 7 days: Incidents (2) with scope 'My district' and stage chips; the card status line answers it without opening.
Optional: open the case file (3) → History tab shows my decision and every step since.

referenceJourneys.task: Find every open incident on I-80 in my district on the map
steps: Tap Map (1) → opens on District 7 with incidents plotted (not Event Groups), open stages selected by default.
Type '80' in the route/PM search (2) — normalised so '80', 'I-80', '080', 'R080' match route 80 only; the list and map filter together and 'Fit to results' frames them.
Hover/select a row to highlight its marker; tap a marker to preview and 'Open case file' if needed (3).

referenceJourneys.persona: GeoTech Engineer (first day; iPad landscape 1024 px in the field, laptop in the office)
referenceJourneys.task: Open the assessment assigned to me and fill out the technical form for the incident, including photos and measurements, then submit it for review
steps: Sign in on the iPad → Home 'My drafts (1)' shows 'Route 101 slide — Assigned by B. Chen 2 days ago · 0 of 12 sections'; tap 'Start form' (1) → Form hub opens, pre-filled from the field report (D/C/R/PM, coordinates, date observed).
Tap 'A Report header' (2), check the prefilled values, 'Save and continue' (3) — autosave also runs; repeat through sections B–I using 'Save and continue' (one tap each: 4-11).
Section 'J Measurements' (12): enter the eight values with unit suffixes; 'Open 3D terrain' only if wanted; 'Save and continue' (13).
Section 'K Notes and actions' (14), then 'L Photos' (15): 'Add photos' → camera/library (16), photos land in the section with Mapped/Heading badges; 'Mark complete' (17).

Hub shows '12 of 12 sections complete'; tap 'Submit for review' (18) → sheet lists completeness and takes the comment to the reviewer; 'Submit' (19). Receipt: 'Sent for review — reviewer A. Patel is next'; one submit advances both the form and the assessment.

referenceJourneys.persona: GeoTech Engineer (first day; iPad landscape 1024 px in the field, laptop in the office)
referenceJourneys.task: Return to a submission that was sent back for correction, understand what the reviewer wants, fix it and resubmit
steps: Home top section 'Returned for changes (1)' quotes A. Patel's comment in full ('Slope height inconsistent with photo 4') with 'Sections flagged: J'; tap 'Open form and fix' (1).

Form hub opens with the quote pinned at the top and section J tagged 'Needs attention'; tap J (2), correct the value (the form is editable because the return moved both records back to draft), 'Save and continue' (3).
Tap 'Resubmit for review' (4), add a reply to the reviewer, confirm (5). Receipt: 'Resubmitted — A. Patel will see what changed since their last review.'

referenceJourneys.persona: GeoTech Engineer (first day; iPad landscape 1024 px in the field, laptop in the office)
referenceJourneys.task: Look at the 3D terrain around the site and create a terrain cross section
steps: From the case file, tap the Site tab (1): 2D map at the site with the point and drawn area; tap 'Open 3D terrain' (2) — the scene loads in place at the site (capability-gated, quality Auto).
Tap 'Draw new cross section' (3) → terrain tool opens at the incident coordinates with the point marked; tap the terrain to place P1, P2 (4-5); 'Build profile' (6).
Profile drawer docks at the bottom with the chart and stats while the terrain stays visible; tap 'Save to Route 101 slide' (7), name it, Save (8).
Back on the Site tab the section appears in 'Cross sections (1)' with a thumbnail; reviewers see it there too.

referenceJourneys.task: See which assessments are waiting for my delegation and delegate one to a branch chief, assigning the engineer directly when I know who should take it

Press 'Send to B. Chen and assign J. Doe' (4); receipt 'Sent — J. Doe is notified and will start the technical form'; the card moves to 'Recently done'.
Home 'To sign off (1)' lists only approved assessments in North GeoTech Office with 'Approved by A. Patel Sep 4'; tap the card (1) to open the Form tab in summary mode and read it (optional).
Tap 'Finalize' (2) → sheet: 'Finalizing closes the assessment record. The incident stays open until engineer J. Doe marks it resolved.' Cancel is focused; press 'Finalize assessment' (3).
Receipt 'Finalized. Next: J. Doe marks the incident resolved.' The case banner reads 'Assessment finalized — incident open'.

referenceJourneys.task: Get a picture of all active assessments in my office and where they are stuck
steps: Home 'My office at a glance' strip shows six counts by step (Awaiting branch 2 · Awaiting engineer 3 · In progress 5 · Under review 4 · Returned 1 · Approved 1).
Tap 'Longest waiting' (1) → Incidents with scope 'My office', open stages, sorted by time in step; each card shows holder and 'In this step 12 days'.
Tap any count chip instead (1) to see that step only; 'Group by Event Group' if needed.

referenceJourneys.persona: Assessment Reviewer who is also Admin (first day, 13-inch laptop)
referenceJourneys.task: Find the assessments submitted for my review, read the technical submission with its photos and map, and approve or return it

Review/submit consistency: make POST /assessments/{id}/review and /submit also set the linked submission status (SUBMITTED, APPROVED, or DRAFT/REJECTED-as-returned) in one transaction, or reject submission-level review when a submission is linked to an assessment. Reason: today two independent state machines produce contradictory screens (assessment REVISION_REQUESTED while form SUBMITTED/locked) and two Approve buttons; states themselves are unchanged.
Names instead of ids: include created_by_name / actor_name on submission summaries and workflow events (assessment events already carry actor_name). Reason: 'User #7' cannot be humanised client-side.

Filters and totals: list_incidents and list_assessments accept district, office_code (exists), route, stage/state (multi) and return total_count with cursor pagination; /event-groups/{id} returns assessment_id and assessment_state per incident. Reason: removes 1000-row client fetches and misleading counts.

Cross-section attachment: add optional incident_id to cross-section projects/records (or auto-create one Project per incident). Reason: sections must attach to the case file; the Project entity stays.

Structured intake inputs: NEEDS_REPORTER_INFORMATION accepts requested_fields[]; DUPLICATE_OR_LINKED already stores duplicate_of_incident_id. Reason: the reporter must see exactly which fields to fix (already a stated must-see).

Optional: per-section completion flags and last-edited section on submissions (or store in a JSON column) so the hub can show 'n of m complete' server-side; client can derive from field completeness in the meantime.
Optional: draft autosave endpoint (PATCH partial submission) if the existing save-draft PUT is too heavy for per-field autosave.

risks: Aggregation performance: until the /case endpoint exists the case file issues several parallel requests; mitigate by lazy-loading tabs and caching the incident list summaries.

Two state machines: if the review-consistency backend change slips, the web must call both endpoints sequentially and handle partial failure with a visible 'form status did not update — retry' notice.
Coordinator habit change: the merged intake sheet and the disappearance of My Work need a one-week overlap and a note on Home ('My Work is now Home').
Deep links and emails: every legacy URL must redirect into the right tab; build the redirect table with tests before removing old pages.

ArcGIS layout sensitivity: SceneView and MapView inside new flex/grid regions must be re-verified against .map-stack-guard and never receive position/z-index on .esri-view; bottom sheets over maps need hit-testing on iPad Safari.

Photo upload from web: the mobile app remains the primary capture tool; if the submission attachment endpoint cannot accept browser multipart, the Evidence tab must state plainly that photos come from the mobile app.
Role data gaps: engineer workload/distance in the picker depends on assignment counts and incident coordinates being available in one call; ship name + office first, load/distance second.
Scope creep in Admin › Routing: the endpoint exists but has no UI today; keep it to a table with one action per row.
Accessibility regressions in custom sheets: the ActionSheet must wrap the existing ModalDialog focus management rather than reimplementing it.
Content cap at 1200 px may feel narrow for table-heavy admin screens on wide monitors; allow 1440 for tables and maps.
deliberatelyDropped: The stacked 'Navigation' card above content below 1024 px and the desktop footer: they cost the first 700 px on phones and tablets and add nothing to any task.

Separate Assessments, Event Groups, Submissions worklist, Mission Center and Terrain Cross Sections destinations: all folded into the case file, the Incidents list filters, the Map and the Site tab; six pages with one rail+detail layout became one object page.

The standalone photo-evidence page: same photos as the library with a second design and a second URL strategy; merged into Evidence with Map mode and lightbox telemetry.
Two-step triage modals with a pre-selected nearest Event Group and two commit buttons: replaced by one decision sheet with explicit choice and one commit.
Duplicate approve/submit controls (submission-level vs assessment-level): one decision per action sheet.
Shared 'Optional workflow notes' textarea, bottom-of-page Submit comment and Reviewer Note: notes live in the action that consumes them.
Raw codes in the UI: role enums in the header, office codes, event codes, stage codes, 'User #id', 'Attachment #id', MIME types, truncated SHA-256, job UUID prefixes, 'Dataset #id'.
Six-decimal coordinates on cards and panels: on the Site tab with a copy button only.
Cross-section 'Project' as a user-facing container: sections belong to the incident.

Raw Geometry JSON textarea and 'Raw Contact Data' debug details: geometry is drawn on the map; debug goes to logs.
Auto-mounted high-quality 3D SceneView for every viewer: 3D is on request and capability-gated.
Eleven always-on ArcGIS widgets on small maps and the always-open Search/Basemap/LayerList expands on the statewide map: one 'Map tools' expand on large screens only.
Hover-only affordances and title-attribute tooltips as the sole carrier of information (file names, timestamps, role codes, photo counts).
Duplicate metrics in the terrain tool (Path/Samples/Spacing/Source coverage shown up to five times) and Esri-internal provenance prose by default.
